decisions.reason: The single-tube air fin cooler sits close to the core offer, so keeping it costs little, and with only one year of evidence its value is still uncertain, which favors keeping the option open.
This condenser variant is cheap to keep alongside the core line and it is too early to judge its demand, though it overlaps with Product C, which slightly raises the chance of consolidation.
This second single-tube condenser overlaps with Product B, so it may be merged into one line, but low holding costs and unresolved uncertainty argue for keeping it for now.
The tube liner supports the growing lifecycle service business, costs little to keep, and could lead to further service growth, so dropping it now would waste option value.
Customized air coolers are central to the firm's integrated-solutions strategy and are built to order, so keeping them costs little while their upside remains open.
Tube end repair inserts complement the spare-parts and repair services at low holding cost, and early evidence gives no reason to abandon them.
